newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER - LEAGUE LEADERS PSV STAY TOP DESPITE DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - LEAGUE LEADERS PSV STAY TOP DESPITE DRAW.

text.p: Dutch league leaders PSV Eindhoven dropped two precious point drawing 2-2 away against NAC Breda on Sunday, but they stayed top of the table as their main rivals Feyenoord also drew 0-0 against Vitesse Arnhem.

Boudewijn Zenden gave PSV an early lead in the 18th minute, but NAC were the dominant tream in the first half, scoring twice in rapid succession through Australian striker Alan Arambasic in the 27th minute and Ruud Brood in the 29th.
PSV emerged after the break as a different team, forcing NAC deep back into their own half and creating several scoring chances as they piled on the pressure.
But Belgian international Gille de Bilde, making his debut for the Eindhoven side, was the only player to find the back of the net, scoring the equaliser from a cross by Zeljko Petrovic.
De Bilde joined PSV from Anderlecht while sitting out a suspension for striking an opponent in the face.
His goal kept PSV at the top of the Dutch first division ahead of Feyenoord by virtue of a superior goal difference. Both sides have 59 points from 27 matches.
Third-placed Twente Enschede, playing lowly RKC Waalwijk, failed to capitalise on the points lost by the top two clubs.

Twente had previously lost only two away matches this season but conceded three goals in 39 minutes due to a chaotic defense. John Bosman scored twice for Twente, but RKC emerged 3-2 winners and passed on the bottom-of-the-table slot to AZ Alkmaar.
Ajax Amsterdam, who have little chance of retaining their league title, beat Volendam 3-0 despite lacking a full attack.

Coach Louis van Gaal decided to rest Marc Overmars ahead of Ajax's first-leg European Cup semi-final match on Wednesday against Juventus. Tijjani Babangide was on duty with the Nigerian national team while Patrick Kluivert, who will miss the Juventus match, was waiting to undergo surgery on a knee injury.
Kiki Musampa scored the opening goal six minutes before half-time.
In the 55th minute Ajax suffered an apparent setback when Jari Litmanen was sent off for kicking a Volendam defender.
But reduced to 10 players the Amsterdammers scored two more goals through Arnold Scholten in the 66th minute and Nordin Wooter in the 83rd.
Ajax are fourth in the league table, trailing the leaders by eleven points with one game in hand.
